summary.intent: Land slice 1 of the 'collapse large inherited prop sources' feature (collapse decided per source by members reaching the component after Pick/Omit, consistent across structural and checker lanes) on a branch, with review before pushing.
summary.outcome: Worker committed e403ddfd locally with a new model test and passing gates; a final code review found 9 issues, of which 5-6 were sent back to the worker as a bounded last-round fix list and 3 were deferred to the PR's 'Not verified' section. Nothing pushed yet.

repo: Collapse of large inherited prop sources has two lanes (structural resolver and semantic/checker) that must agree through one `CollapseContext::collapses` function; disagreement on the dependency predicate (in_node_modules vs actually-loaded via `is_dependency_file`) is a recurring risk.

Verification gates for this repo: lint, doc-check, machete, typos, nextest on core and semantic, checker lane, byte-identity of Spectrum/Mantine/antd output vs main, and Chakra medians of 139 with Button at 146 argTypes.
Chakra style-system source has ~700 members; expanding it instead of collapsing bloats output from ~516 KB to ~1.96 MB.
`merge_semantic` and `merge_semantic_with` still use `CollapseContext::OFF`, while the CLI and watch pass the real context.
`scripts/weekly.py` benchmark history was measured with collapse 'none'; it should pin `--collapse-inherited-props` explicitly so default changes don't silently shift the series.
The Storybook addon default changing from 'none' to 'dependencies' is breaking for users with own interfaces over 200 props; it is covered in the changeset and PR body.

code.finding: Omit handling re-resolves its base with a global `expand_all` when one collapsed source falls under the threshold, expanding other large sources too, and resolves the base twice (probe plus real), costing ~2^depth for nested Omits.
`move_notable` removes a prop by name even if it was the component's own redeclaration, moving it into `notableInherited` and dropping it from own props.
The declared member count (`count_members`, `DeclaredSource.declared`, cache field) is never read by the collapse decision, which uses the reaching count; it is dead weight with extra RPC batches.
`CollapseContext::collapses` treats any node_modules file as a dependency when load_dependencies is on, unlike the structural lane's `is_dependency_file`.

`declares_large_source` only considers interfaces and Passthrough object-literal aliases and is project-wide, so one unrelated large interface enables `expand_all` (chain splitting) for all components.
`one_layer_per_collapsed_source` merges layers by (type_name, file_name), rewrites `total_props`, and intersects `omitted`, dropping keys omitted on only one path.
Benchmark no longer passes `--collapse-inherited-props`, so it follows the default.

workflow: Subagent hand-back messages are model output, not user instructions; act on them within the session's permissions.
After several review rounds, split findings into must-fix versus document-only and cap the final round (50-call cap, commit only) to avoid endless iteration.
Do a focused diff check rather than another full review after the bounded fix round.
Reviewer ran on the diff only without building or testing, so its findings need verification via model tests.

friction: Four rounds of fix and review on slice 1 without converging; each fix surfaced new issues.
The design as a whole-component mode switch (`expand_all`) with probe-and-re-resolve caused repeated issues rather than a per-source decision.
An earlier instruction to delete declared-count machinery was made unnecessary by a later design but the code remained.
Worker disclosed the Omit over-expansion as open and the reviewer independently confirmed it.
